info.name: Moderation Service
info.description:
Every HTTP endpoint of the Moderation Service (Team 18, PAD project "Student ID, Please"), ordered as a walkthrough of one shift: seed three applicants, call them, look the calls up, revise one of them, read the shift summary, then clean up.

Run it top to bottom with the Collection Runner against a running stack (`docker compose up -d`). Each request asserts its own status code, and the ids are passed between requests through collection variables.

**Setup** creates its own applicants, because Moderation only judges applicants that really exist: `POST /moderation/decide` answers `404 NOT_FOUND` for an unknown id. Each applicant gets a profile in Applicant Service, a university record in University Record Service and a credential from Credential Service, which is what the four dependencies are then asked about:

- the **clean** applicant is enrolled, never banned and holds an honest credential
- the **forged** applicant holds a credential issued with `scenario: fake_student_id`, so it comes back `valid: false` with `FORGED_SIGNATURE`
- the **banned** applicant has a university record with `previouslyBanned: true`

The verdict assertions are deliberately about internal consistency - `correct` agrees with `decision == expectedDecision`, a correct call costs nothing, a wrong one costs something - rather than hardcoding a verdict per applicant. That way the collection stays green while the dependencies' own rules change. At the time of writing Server Rules Service reports `NO_PREVIOUS_BAN` as violated for every applicant, which makes `expectedDecision` `ban` for all three; once that is fixed the clean applicant scores `accept` and the forged one `reject`, and these same assertions still hold.

The collection is re-runnable: the first request under **Decisions** gives each run its own `sessionId` (`shift-<timestamp>`), because the service records one decision per applicant per session and would otherwise answer `409` on a second run. **Cleanup** removes the applicants and records it created, so re-running does not pile them up.

item.name: Setup
item.description: Creates the three applicants this collection judges. Moderation holds no applicants of its own: it reads them from Applicant, Credential, Server Rules and University Record, and refuses to judge an id none of them knows. These requests go to those services through the Gateway, with the same player token as everything else.

request.description: An enrolled student with nothing against them. POST /applicants/generate is not used: it is an internal-only route and the Gateway no longer exposes it, and a generated applicant is random where this one has to be known in advance.

exec: // One student id per applicant per run. The format is FCIM- plus six digits;
// anything else is reported as MALFORMED_STUDENT_ID by Credential Service.
// They are not shared between runs, so two runs never collide on an identity.
pm.test('it came back with the identity this run asked for', function () {
// Moderation is asked about this id below. It is a UUID the service assigns,
// never one the collection picks, so it has to be captured here.

item.name: Give the clean applicant a university record

request.description: Without a record the applicant cannot be confirmed to exist at the university, which on its own is enough for the evidence to call for a closer look. previouslyBanned is false and isEnrolled is true, so nothing here speaks against them.

body.raw:
{
    "applicantId": "{{cleanApplicant}}",
    "name": "Postman Clean Student",
    "studentId": "{{cleanStudentId}}",
    "role": "student_faf",
    "university": "Technical University of Moldova",
    "faculty": "FCIM",
    "program": "Software Engineering",
    "studyYear": 3,
    "status": "active",
    "averageGrade": 9.1,
    "previouslyBanned": false,
    "isEnrolled": true
}
